sections.content: This course mainly focuses on the 6 supply chain drivers and metrics, which is facilities, inventory, transportation, information, sourcing and pricing. Unlike ISOM3710, Microsoft Excel is not required, but you still have to do some calculations. There are a few case studies and simulation games in class to facilitate your learning. Group project exists but it is not complicated.
sections.teaching:
Prof. is very nice and teaches clearly. Sometimes it may be hard to catch up the content when she is talking about formulas, but she will upload full version ppt after class so don't worry.
There are always students asking her questions after class, and she is willing to answer any questions, including those about group projects.
If she recognise you, and you are in the marginal cases, she may help you raise a sub-grade. So although she seldom check attendance, it is good to attend every lesson.
Regarding to attendance, as my session is 9am, few people come to class on time, so she sometimes pass the attendance sheet at the first few minutes of class. Maybe it helps, but who knows?

sections.content:
For course content, please refer to the syllabus attached.
Generally speaking, the course is about the six drivers (i.e. Inventory, Facility, Transportation, Information, Pricing, Sourcing) affecting the supply chain efficiency and responsiveness, also their tradeoffs. A couple of cases and examples are introduced to facilitate students' understandings on the operations level of different drivers (e.g. Zara, 7-11). Also, you will have chances to implement what you have learnt in 3 different simulation games. You will find it interesting since you are not just learning concepts/textbook facts, you can also try to apply them and figure out the positive/negative consequences. The applications of Math involved in this course are quite simple. All of the calculations are based on newsvendor model and EOQ model (as mentioned in ISOM2700). No worries if you are weak in Math.
sections.teaching: Professor Wang is excellent in teaching. She explained everything in a very detailed and organized way. The lecture time is managed very well and nothing would be missed during lectures. You will surely understand all the concepts if you attended all the lectures with concentration.

With increasing competition around the globe, supply chain management is both a challenge and an opportunity for companies. The objective of this course is to introduce you to the key concepts and techniques that will allow you to analyze, manage and improve supply chain processes for different industries and markets.
